Refuse verbs on a zero-column table that has rows

Source: R/execute.R
check_zero_column_input.Rd

A cudf table with no columns always has 0 rows, so a zero-column tbl_gpu carries its row count on the R side (x$nrow, see new_tbl_gpu()). Verbs lower to cudf calls that cannot see it, so running one on such a table would silently return a table with the wrong row count. Until zero-column tables are supported by every verb, fail loudly instead. Called by push_op(), push_join() (both sides), the binds and vec_proxy(); summarise() and the slice() family handle this input before it reaches push_op().

Usage

check_zero_column_input(.data, input_schema, verb)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu

input_schema

current_schema(.data)

verb

Character, the node type, for the message
